subtitle: Lesson 10 · Cloud Encryption: At Rest and In Transit

code:
Azure Key Vault

  Keys          -> encrypt / decrypt data
  Secrets       -> connection strings, API keys
  Certificates  -> TLS certs

One service. Three distinct jobs.
caption: Apps call Key Vault to create a key — it generates, stores, and guards it.

code:
AWS KMS (Key Management Service)

  Keys only -> generate, store, control use

  Secrets    -> AWS Secrets Manager (separate)
  Certs      -> AWS Certificate Manager (separate)
caption: KMS is deliberately scoped to encryption keys; AWS splits the rest out.

steps.sub: create a key with real hardware randomness

steps.label: Store
steps.sub: inside a hardware vault your code never touches

steps.label: Rotate & Gate
steps.sub: replace on schedule, check every request first

eyebrow: How an app actually uses it
code:
App  ->  KeyVault.Decrypt(ciphertext)  ->  plaintext

The app never downloads the raw key.
Only the SERVICE touches the key material.
caption: A stolen app secret is far less damaging than a stolen raw key.
